recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-24077 unless a future work group decision changes the UDIEntryType canonical URL or binding policy more broadly.
issue_request: FHIR-24077 was a Published FHIR-core Device change request resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5. It requested a UDIEntryType code electronic-transmission with display Electronic Transmission and a definition for UDI information received electronically from the device through a communication protocol, and it rejected changing the binding target from the complete ValueSet to a CodeSystem URL.
initial_application: Commit 439f71f7090850848dd0d27c1800c89b4056edf7 explicitly listed 24077 and added electronic-transmission to the Device.udiCarrier.entryType list in the then-authoritative Device spreadsheet. Commit 7425b11c1a793b942c2f1e51782da0d1165d6961 corrected the full entryType list and added the electronic-transmission concept display and definition. Later source rework preserved the content in XML terminology and StructureDefinition source.
additional_context: Device is active in source/fhir.ini, source/device/codesystem-udi-entry-type.xml contains the electronic-transmission code, and Device.udiCarrier.entryType is required-bound to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/udi-entry-type. OO minutes from 2019-10-31 record FHIR-24077 in the accepted Device block vote as Persuasive with mod. Direct Zulip and Confluence key searches found no conflicting later community evidence. FHIR-23848 appeared nearby because it concerns Device protocol/Bluetooth mappings, but it is a separate mapping issue.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because the active current source already implements the requested code, display, definition, and required ValueSet binding semantics, while changing the URL/binding would contradict the accepted modification.
